drhp.business: Waterways operates overnight ocean and coastal cruises in India under the Cordelia Cruises brand through a single vessel, the 'MV Empress' (796 cabins, up to ~2,005 guests), sailing domestic destinations (Mumbai, Goa, Kochi, Chennai, Lakshadweep, Visakhapatnam, Puducherry) and international itineraries (Sri Lanka, Maldives, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia). Revenue comes from cabin tickets plus onboard spend (dining, casino, spa, entertainment, MICE/weddings); critical operations (F&B, housekeeping, crewing, entertainment) are outsourced.
drhp.end_markets: Indian leisure/luxury cruise guests and international travellers visiting India|Direct bookings 62.25% (FY26), 62.98% (FY25), 59.96% (FY24) of cabins; balance via travel agents
drhp.expansion: Waterways intends to expand beyond its single vessel by introducing two additional cruise vessels, 'Norwegian Sky' (capacity up to 2,004 guests) and 'Norwegian Sun' (up to 1,936 guests), and to add new domestic and international itineraries (including Colombo, Sri Lanka and Male, Maldives from Kochi from October 2026), while upgrading dining, cabins and entertainment to meet growing Indian cruise demand supported by the Cruise Bharat Mission.

business_ops.seasonality: Cruise demand is seasonal and sensitive to travel demand, fuel prices and geopolitical conditions; the India cruise market is estimated to have declined ~12% in Fiscal 2026 on macro/fuel/geopolitical headwinds. During monsoon (challenging west-coast sea conditions) the homeport is relocated to Chennai; festive periods (Christmas, New Year) carry special events. Operational metrics: passenger load factor 84.99% (FY26), 91.63% (FY25), 78.54% (FY24); average ticket price Rs 10,979.86 (FY26); revenue per passenger (APD) Rs 12,036.39 (FY26); fuel cost per passenger cruise day Rs 1,480.33 (FY26).
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset structure: vessel MV Empress owned via wholly-owned subsidiary Bay Cruise Investment Inc.; two new vessels (Norwegian Sky, Norwegian Sun) chartered from step-down subsidiary Baycruise Shipping and Leasing (IFSC) Private Limited under Time Charter Agreements. Critical cruise operations (food & beverage, housekeeping, crewing, entertainment) are outsourced to third parties to enable scalability and manage seasonal demand. Key third-party service providers named: SA Cruise Services Limited, Apollo Export Warehouse LLC (with Indian arm Asturias Ship Chandlers Private Limited), Campbell Cruise & Yacht Management Limited and Wizcraft Entertainment Agency Private Limited. Direct bookings supported by a 148-person call-centre team.

Entire fresh issue funds lease payments to a related step-down subsidiary (Baycruise IFSC) rather than direct asset ownership; related-party transactions were 14-20% of revenue in FY24-FY25.
Industry cyclicality (India cruise market declined ~12% in FY26) and fuel-price/geopolitical sensitivity.

Income-tax disallowance of Rs 582.20 million of FY23 'exceptional items' (tax liability Rs 146.53 million) under appeal, plus a TAMP Passenger Facilitation Charges dispute (Rs 120.96 million deposited).

strengths_observed: Leading domestic ocean cruise operator in India (Cordelia Cruises) with approximately 79% value market share in Fiscal 2025 (CRISIL) and 730,819 guests carried since launch.

Large under-penetrated market opportunity: India cruise penetration ~0.01% vs ~5.7% in North America, with the market projected to grow at ~20-25% CAGR to Rs 18,200-22,500 million by Fiscal 2031 and government support via the Cruise Bharat Mission.

High direct-booking mix (~62% of cabins in FY26) reducing agent commissions and supporting margins; experienced cruise-industry management led by the Indian Cruise Lines Association's founding member.
Strong FY25 operating metrics: 91.63% passenger load factor and EBITDA of Rs 2,154.59 million (36% margin); improving net worth from negative FY24 to Rs 802.04 million (FY26).
Defined fleet-growth pathway via two chartered vessels (Norwegian Sky by FY27, Norwegian Sun by FY28) and new itineraries (Colombo, Male from Kochi).
